at betale sig.explanation: "At betale sig" means "to pay off (be worth it)". To say what is worth doing, use "det" (it) and add "at" and a verb: "Det betaler sig at lære dansk" (It pays off to learn Danish). Do not mix it up with "at betale" (to pay money): "Jeg betaler regningen" (I pay the bill).

at betale tilbage.explanation: "At betale tilbage" means "to pay back". When you say what money you pay back, put it before "tilbage": "Jeg betaler pengene tilbage" (I pay the money back). To name the person who gets the money, put the person straight after "betale": "Jeg betaler dig tilbage" (I pay you back).

at betegne.explanation: "At betegne" means "to denote / describe". When you say what a word stands for, say "Ordet 'bil' betegner et køretøj" (The word 'bil' stands for a vehicle).

at betjene.explanation: "At betjene" means "to serve / operate". When someone works a machine, say "Han betjener kranen" (He operates the crane). When a waiter brings food to a table, use "at servere" (to serve): "Tjeneren serverer maden" (The waiter serves the food).

at betragte.explanation: "At betragte" means "to regard / consider". When you look at something calmly for a while, it means "to watch": "Hun betragter solnedgangen" (She watches the sunset).

at betro.explanation: "At betro" means "to confide". To confide in someone, add "sig" (yourself) and "til" (to): "Hun betroede sig til sin søster" (She confided in her sister). When you hand something important to a person you trust, it means "to entrust": "Jeg betror ham nøglerne" (I entrust him with the keys).

at betvivle.explanation: "At betvivle" means "to question / doubt". It is built from "at tvivle" (to doubt). No small word follows it: "Jeg betvivler hans ord" (I doubt his word). "At tvivle" needs "på" (on) instead: "Jeg tvivler på hans ord" (I doubt his word).

at betyde.explanation: "At betyde" means "to mean". When something is important to you, say "Det betyder meget for mig" (It means a lot to me). When you explain what follows from something, say "Det betyder, at vi må vente" (That means that we must wait).

at beundre.explanation: "At beundre" means "to admire". When you look at something beautiful with delight, say "Vi beundrer udsigten" (We admire the view). Do not mix it up with "at kunne lide" (to like): "Jeg kan lide min nabo" (I like my neighbor).

at bevare.explanation: "At bevare" means "to preserve / keep". To say you stay calm, use "at bevare roen" (to keep calm): "Han bevarer roen" (He keeps calm). To keep a thing you own, use "at beholde" (to keep): "Jeg beholder bogen" (I keep the book).

at bevilge.explanation: "At bevilge" means "to grant". To say that money has been granted, say "Der er bevilget to millioner kroner" (Two million kroner have been granted).

at bevise.explanation: "At bevise" means "to prove". When you show that something is true, say "Hun beviste, at det var sandt" (She proved that it was true). When you show what you can do, use "at bevise sit værd" (to prove your worth): "Han ville bevise sit værd" (He wanted to prove his worth).

at bevæge.explanation: "At bevæge" means "to move". To move yourself, add "sig" (yourself): "Han bevæger sig langsomt" (He moves slowly). To move house, use "at flytte" (to move): "Vi flytter til Odense" (We are moving to Odense).

at bevæge sig.explanation: "At bevæge sig" means "to move". When you move your own body, say "Han bevæger sig langsomt" (He moves slowly). To carry a thing to another place, use "at flytte" (to move): "Jeg flytter bordet" (I am moving the table).

at bide.explanation: "At bide" means "to bite". When an insect bites you, say "Myggen bed mig" (The mosquito bit me). To bite into food, add "i" (in): "Hun bider i æblet" (She bites into the apple). Do not mix it up with "at bede" (to ask / pray), which looks similar: "Jeg beder om hjælp" (I ask for help).

at bidrage.explanation: "At bidrage" means "to contribute". To say what you give to, add "til" (to): "Hun bidrager til forskningen" (She contributes to the research).

at binde.explanation: "At binde" means "to tie / bind". When you tie hair up, add "op" (up): "Jeg binder håret op" (I tie my hair up).

at binde snørebånd.explanation: "At binde snørebånd" means "to tie shoelaces". It is built from "at binde" (to tie) and "snørebånd" (shoelaces). To tie a scarf, use the same verb: "Jeg binder et tørklæde" (I tie a scarf).

at bistå.explanation: "At bistå" means "to assist". It is the verb for "en bistand" (assistance). To say who gets the help, put the person after the verb: "Revisoren bistår firmaet" (The accountant assists the company).

at blaffe.explanation: "At blaffe" means "to hitchhike". To ask for a ride, say "Må jeg få en lift?" (Can I get a ride?)

at blande.explanation: "At blande" means "to mix". To mix two things together, add "med" (with): "Han blander mælk med kaffe" (He mixes milk with coffee). Do not mix it up with "at blande sig" (to interfere): "Bland dig ikke i det" (Stay out of it).

at blande sig.explanation: "At blande sig" means "to interfere". To say what you interfere in, add "i" (in): "Du skal ikke blande dig i andres liv" (You should not interfere in other people's lives). Without "sig" (yourself), "at blande" means "to mix": "Jeg blander saft og vand" (I mix cordial and water).

at blegne.explanation: "At blegne" means "to fade". It is built from "bleg" (pale). When a face turns white, it means "to go pale": "Hun blegnede af skræk" (She went pale with fear).

at blinke.explanation: "At blinke" means "to blink / wink". When stars or lights shine on and off, say "Stjernerne blinker" (The stars are twinkling). When a driver signals a turn, say "Han blinker til venstre" (He signals left).

at blive.explanation: "At blive" means "to become / stay". When something changes, say "Det bliver koldt i aften" (It will get cold tonight). When you do not leave, say "Jeg bliver hjemme" (I stay at home). When you say what will happen, say "Det bliver godt" (It will be good). Do not mix it up with "at være" (to be): "Han er læge" (He is a doctor).
